items.text: You can't rest your way out of burnout. If the demands stay the same, the exhaustion does too. Recovery isn't pushing through or a smarter self-care routine — it's dropping the load long enough to rebuild. Rested and still wrecked isn't failure.
items.rationale: Angle 1. Reframes burnout as a load problem, not an effort problem, and names the shame of 'I rested and I'm still broken.' High recognition for late-diagnosed adults; defensible against the source's core claim without overstating.

items.text: A late diagnosis isn't only relief. There's grief too — for the years of not knowing, for the kid who white-knuckled through without any support. You don't have to choose between the two. Most people hold both at once, and that's the honest version.
items.rationale: Angle 4. Validates the grief the 'diagnosis = liberation' narrative erases, holding grief and relief together rather than competing. Speaks to an experience, not for everyone; evergreen framing so source is supporting, not a hard factual hook.

items.text: When the building itself is the barrier — strip lighting, open-plan noise, all-day masking — what does 'reasonable accommodation' even mean? For a lot of neurodivergent workers, remote was never a perk. It was access. Strict 5-day RTO isn't a neutral policy.
items.rationale: Angle 8. Framed as a question to open discussion and give people advocacy language, avoiding pure outrage. Says 'a lot of' not 'all' to avoid speaking for everyone.
items.sensitivity_flag: The disproportionate-pushout claim rests on a 2025 reporting anchor; the post is written as an evergreen reframe and makes no breaking-news claim, but if reused, don't present the data as current 2026 reporting.
